title: The Howards and McCulloughs, and the church behind his house
summary: Willard reads an article about the two church music families and the small church behind Howard's home.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: And it says here that there were two outstanding musical families active in church musical affairs --the Howards and the McCulloughs.
And it said, 'The Howards and the McCulloughs' was a commonly heard phrase. Behind Paul Howard's
* Cipio, with one 'p', is the common spelling.

home on 92nd Street in Los Angeles, there is still a small, white church where Negroes still gather to sing. And Paul said, with his eyes twinkling, 'You should hear them.' I asked if they used instruments, and he said, 'Yes.drums, trombone, washboard, perhaps four or five tambourines with handclapping.'
That's the church that's right here.
Behind this house, here. So the McCulloughs--were they--that was in Los Angeles, that was a Los Angeles family?

Yep, some of 'em. Only thing you can do--I don't know this fellow who got that one up, but they're tryin' to--I don't know, the only thing you can do to it is add to it, you can't take nothin' away from it. No, ma'am.

Well, this gives us some information --Getting to read this article gives us some information we didn't have before, and things that we can talk to you about. And also, sometime, some things get in print that aren't quite right. And so, it's kinda' good to check 'em out with you, and find out if everything we have here is the way it really happened.
Well, I don't know. I can't tell you. All I know is--Susie knows as much about my brother and them as anybody. My wife does . But he didn't play nothin'. I mean, he played somethin', but he wadn't--
He didn't get too good--naw, he didn't like it that well.
